> [{"id":6110,"total":3,"profit":[]},{"id":6111,"total":3,"profit":[]},{"id":6112,"total":5,"profit":[]},{"id":6113,"total":6,"profit":[]},{"id":6114,"total":1,"profit":[]},{"id":6115,"total":22,"profit":[{"id":1637238,"r":9,"n":0,"b":"Tactics (10m, most of it will apply to 25m as well)\n\nI'm assuming you are familiar with the normal mode and decked out in heroic gear by now (you need to kill the first 6 bosses in heroic mode to unlock this encounter, this fact actually cost us one ID).\n\nThe differences to normal mode are:\n\n- As usual, all HP and damage dealt is increased significantly, most importantly the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=56575]Burning Tendons[/url] have too much hp to kill them within one phase. This fact alone roughly doubles the time you'll need for the encounter.\n- Everytime an amalgation spawns, if debuffs a single player (10) / some players (25) with [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106199]Blood Corruption: Death[/url]. Dispelling this debuff makes it jump to another player and has a chance to transform it into [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106200]Blood Corruption: Earth[/url]. When this debuff fades, the player will be granted [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106213]Blood of Neltharion[/url].\n- Everytime you kill an amalgation (rolling it off does NOT count), the raid gets a stack of [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106005]Degradation[/url].\n- The killed blood will slowly crawl to the next opening and respawn.\n\nThese facts lead to the following general tactic changes:\n\n- You MUST optimize tendon DPS. While the latest nerfs do not make crazy class stacking a must anymore, you still need decent DPS on them. Therefore, use classes / specs that can burst like crazy every two minutes, use a target makro for your opening spell (/tar boss2 /tar boss3 /cast AwesomeNukeSpell) and get a decent rotation for the 18s window (genereal rule: Use CDs before the damage starts, debuffs first, then short CDs (if you can use them twice this way). Also, your tank's DPS matter a lot here too (Feral Druids are golden, as usual).\n- Do not kill any amalgations you don't have to kill, do not spawn any amalgations you don't have to spawn.\n- Dispell [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106199]Blood Corruption: Death[/url] very fast, do not dispell [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106200]Blood Corruption: Earth[/url] ever. While it might be nice if it jumps to the tanks, there's a chance for it to become [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106199]Blood Corruption: Death[/url] again, wiping you. Not worth the risk anymore.\n- Be fast in preparing the Amalgations. While Tendon DPS are more important, Amalgation DPS really matters a lot.\n\nNow for a concrete tactic:\n\n[b]1st plate:[u][/u][/b]\nWhen the encounter starts, dps three Corruptions asap. Roll em off immediately, spawn a forth one. Tank them on the left/right side of the plate you want to blow up while your second tank tanks and kills the blood on the other side of the plate your want to blow up. When the Amalgation is at ten percent and you have at least 9 bloods, load it up, kill it right there, dps the tendon, spawn the next Amalgation and repeat. \n\n[b]2nd plate:[u][/u][/b]\nKill two Corruptions, roll em off immediately while dispelling. If possible, load them with the remaining blood pools right before the roll, reducing the amount of blood you have to deal with. Repeat the process from the 1st plate. Your tank will probably not be able to kill all the blood alone anymore, help him out. Don't kite yet. \n\n[b]3rd plate:[u][/u][/b]\nNow the &*!@ hits the fan, your offtank will probably tank a lot of blood (10+) right now, two new Corruptions have spawned. Kill two Corruptions, let your Amalgation tank pick up these Amalgations and kite them near your blood Tank. Throw every single survival CD your raid has and nuke away all the blood, roll off the amalgations right afterwards after they've eaten all the blood. If you time it nicely, they won't tick for a single time and you have some free air now. Repeat the process from the first plates, but some things change: Your blood tank will have to start kiting roughly during the first lift-off (or right after) and won't really return to help you. So assign one DPS to regularly kill blood near to your healers and have your Amalgation Tank taunt every roaming blood he sees (its fine to tank 10-15 while tanking the Amalgation). Use heroism/bl and pots for the first liftoff, repeat it with even more blood, pray to the gods and go to town.\n\n[u]Learning process:[/u]\n\nWhile I can only estimate how hard this encounter was before the nerf, now it seemed quite fair to me: No real random elements, you can decide how to manage everything thrown at you and there actually are some options. For our raid, the main difficulty was to not get eaten alive after the first liftoff of the last plate. The key to it was NOT to dps the amalgation like mad but to sacrifice one DD to blow up the blood threatening the healers. Furthermore, we really profited from NOT timing the grips and the liftoffs except for the last plate because our Tendon DPS was by far sufficient even with nuking someone out of a grip during a liftoff (something that most probably was impossible before the nerf). I'm still unsure if it is a viable tactic to not kill two Corruptions after a liftoff but one (saves some time, costs you a Blood of Neltharion). We never tried it, but it might work for you if your DPS is lacking but your healers shine. \nAnother alternative is to use heroism for the last amalgation if you are very confident in your tendon dps. This gives you roughly 10s of time but makes the last tendon dps phase even more challenging. We did that on our first kill after having a 0.2% wipe with that tactic that would probably have been a kill otherwise, so once again: your call :-)\nThe third alternative is to NOT kite any blood but tank and spank the last phase. This is only possible with a very decently equipped block tank (a feral or dk will probably be eaten alive by 25+ bloods). We didn't really dare using this tactic.\nThe forth alternative is to one-tank the whole encounter. I don't really think this is benefical at all, but once more, some guilds did it, so it might work for you if you hit some kind of a brick wall with your dps but your tank is a semi-god.\n\nUpdate:\nwith the 30% nerf up now and the 35% nerf pending, the easiest tactic seems to be to single-tank and dual heal the encounter as you will then easily be able to finish a plate within a single liftoff. While this feels a little less controlled (you have to randomly kill the bloods instead of really tanking them), it boils the encounter down to 6 minutes, you don't get debuffed as much (and have a lot more HP in the last phase) and finally won't even have to deal with as much blood as before (as of course there does not spawn nearly as much blood in 6 minutes). Give it a try if you are still struggling.\n\nLast but not least:\nHave fun!"}]},{"id":6116,"total":17,"profit":[{"id":1652054,"r":11,"n":2,"b":"Tactics for 10m heroic:\n\n[b]Setup[/b]:\nWhile 2T2H is possible, I recommend 2T3H as it allows less careful play. You won't have any dps problems if you were able to beat spine anyway.\n\n[b]Changes from normal mode:[/b]\nTwice on each platform during the first phase, a random non-tank will get infected by a [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=108649]Corrupting Parasite[/url]. After the debuff fades, a [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=57479]Parasite[/url] will spawn at the location of the player and start channeling a 10s spell called [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=108813]Unstable Corruption[/url]. Basically, he'll explode for the hp he has left divided by 10 when he finishes the cast. Two additional notes: Upon spawning, the Parasite kills nearby players, so there should be none near the infected player (the infected player himself does not die, ofc). Secondly, the time zone will slow down the cast to 15s.\n\nFurthermore, the Bloods spawn a lot earlier on the platforms (right after the first impale hit).\n\nIn phase two, DW will spawn [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=57798]Congealing Bloods[/url] when he reaches 15, 10 or 5% hp. These adds won't do anything but run to DW and heal him by one percent each when they reach him. \n\n[u][b]Tactics:[/b][/u]\n\n[b]Platform order:[/b]\nThe \"normal\" platform order (Ysera (green), Alexstrasza (red), Nozdormu (gold), Kalecgos (blue)) is optimal for 2T3H setups. If you are completely unable to get enough survival cooldowns for your tanks, you might change Ysera and Alexstrasza.\n\n[b]Dealing with the Parasite:[/b]\n\nOn the first three platforms, place the parasite in the time zone. If your ranged DPS are able to bring it below 30% on their own, don't bother using melees for it (unless it's a melee that spawned it, then he should help out). If the parasite is below 30%, ignore it and kill the big tentacle instead, the explosion will not deal as much damage as the tentacle does.\n\n[b]Surviving the last platform:[/b]\n\nOn Kalecgos' platform, the !@#$ hits the fan: You don't have a time zone left and you're missing the haste buff and several other benefits of the aspects. The damage requirements on this platform are rather high compared to the first three. To get through this, you should place the first parasite near the tentacle to allow every dps to switch to it fast. Burn it down (BL/Heroism plus pots are not a bad choice here). Soon afterwards you will be forced to retreat to the leg as the bolt will impact. Use some your damage reducing cds and raid cds here, finish the bolt and the tentacle while placing the second parasite near the leg. Finish the tentacle and the parasite combined with the bloods and go for the leg. This is a rather hard damage race as you'll have to deal with the leg tentacles twice and it is a rather bad idea to dps the leg below 90% before everything else is finished (your healers are stressed enough). \n\n[b]Phase 2:[/b]\n\nThe good thing about the nerfs (we're at 15% as I'm writing this) is that you have so much time left to beat the enrage timer that you can finish everything on its own: DPS DW until the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=56724]Fragments[/url] spawn, finish them, finish the[url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=56710] Terrors [/url]in the time zone, drop DW below 16%, go for the bloods, return to DW, stop at 12%, kill Fragments and Terrors a second time, drop DW below 11%, go for the bloods, drop DW below 6%, go for the bloods, offtank / dream-use anything and kill him. The only difficult thing about this phase is to reliably slow the Bloods and kill them off fast enough and to go to this phase solidly (after all, it's almost 12 minutes into the fight). While arguably Spine is harder (I'm not that sure about that after the nerfs), take this encounter seriously or you'll wipe a lot more than you expected, wasting just another 12-minute-try. \n\n\n[b]Tanking:[/b] \n[b]P1:[/b]\nThe tank cooldowns for impale are one of the make-or-breaks of the fight. As Impale deals 840k damage and is NOT mitigated by armor, you'll need decent cooldowns for every single one of them. There are tricks around this by using immunity classes, but they are rather difficult to pull off, so you're a lot better with a \"decent\" tank-eats-it tactic. Each platform will take less than 3 minutes, so do your napkin math and assign a perfect cooldown order for all the platforms. Usually, the tank that takes the first Impale will go for the bloods afterwards and pull them whereever it is you need damage.\n\n[b]P2:[/b]\nTank the big tentacles in the time zone, mark one of them immediately. Help out with the bloods as good as you can, your DPS really matters a lot here. \n\n[b]DPSing:[/b]\n[b]P1:[/b]\nThe tentacle is the most important target on each platform unless you are on the parasite. You should be quite familiar with the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106039]spell weaving[/url] mechanic. As your tank will hopefully bring the bloods to your current target, spread some dots on them to profit from spell weaving. Place yourself decently to avoid triple-hits by the tentacle's slash.\nControl your dps on the leg/arm, especially on platform 3 (do not go below 85% before the tentacle) and 4. (do not go below 95% before the tentacle). Use dream / damage reduces for the second arm-tentacles. Your healers will love you!\n[b]P2:[/b]\nControlled dps and using spell weaving are the key. You need to spread dots and cleave wherever necessary, and you need a reliable slow for the congealing bloods alongside insane burst AoE. \n\n[b]Healing:[/b]\n[b]P1:[/b]\nHelp out the tanks with impale, time your heavy group cds so that you are able to survive the harder parts of platform 3 and 4 (namely the arm tentacles and the bolt impact).\n[b]P2:[/b]\nKeep those tanks alive during [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=106730]Tetanus[/url]. Threaten your stupid DPS to use dream when they still have it after the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=56724]Fragments.[/url]\n\n\nHave fun and see you in Pandaria!"}]},{"id":6128,"total":48,"profit":[{"id":2065438,"r":54,"n":4,"b":"Easy solo as hunter.\n\n1)  Misdirect boss to pet, put a couple hits in.  Do not kill.\n\n2)  When Void ball spawns: chase it down, standing on top of it, it will change directions, do it 11 times just to be safe.  \n\n3)  Nuke boss down after.  \n\n4)  ?\n\n5)  Profit - Achievement Completed."}]}]

If you were wondering what mechanics are still relevant at level 90 for this raid during a quick run through, here you go.\r\n\r\nMagmaw: Kill adds. Kill boss.\r\n\r\nOmnotron: Do not damage the shielded guy - had no problems with this. \r\n\r\nAtramedes: DO NOT get 100 sound (especially the breath), as he will still kill you even at 90 very quickly. Not like that happend to me, though, as I'm very careful... 'cough'\r\n\r\nChimaeron: You need to activate the Bile-O-Tron, or Massacre will insta-kill you. We only had to face one massacre thanks to our DPS, but we survived by all popping our healthstones IMMEDIATELY after. The prot pallies healed themselves up, while I used drain life.\r\n\r\nMaloriak: Burn before adds.\r\n\r\nNefarian: Burn Onyxia, have OT grab adds, don't DPS them. Make sure that everyone knows to go to which of the three platforms to shred the Nova-casting mobs - otherwise, as on our first phase transition, everybody died except the tanks and me - they just popped cooldowns and ran through the lava to the other platforms, while I drain-life + healthstoned to keep myself alive. We downed the boss shortly thereafter just the three of us, though the adds were starting to put the hurt on our OT.  \r\n\r\nHope this helps!"}]}{"id":4850,"comments":[{"id":1086569,"r":5,"n":1,"b":"It is confirmed that Cho'Gall will be the final boss of Bastion of Twilight.\n\nCould it Possibly be? Al'akir is the final boss of the Skywall.\r\n\r\nI hope he will be as tough as Ragnaros."},{"id":1079482,"r":-2,"n":0,"b":"Djin Council - this remind me of [i]Majlis al Jinn [/i]([i]arabic[/i]: [i]Council of Djin[/i]) a huge cave in Oman believed to be meeting place of [url=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genie]Djin[/url] (also known as Genie)"},{"id":1086567,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"The Windlord Itself"},{"id":1102531,"r":-2,"n":0,"b":"The (WIP) confirms that there will be more than the 2 bosses listed"},{"id":1119269,"r":0,"n":0,"b":"If he's immune to nature damage them shammys are doomed :'("},{"id":1129147,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"I have a feeling this achievment won't be very easy during the first few patches of cata :O :S"}]}{"id":5094,"comments":[{"id":1144116,"r":-4,"n":0,"b":"Was this that third Jormungar outside of the colisseum?"},{"id":1284839,"r":17,"n":0,"b":"Differences on heroic: Every 35 seconds, Nefarian summons a new add known as a Blazing Animated Skeleteon ( or Construct, don't remember exactly) that leave a lethal fire patch on the ground that deals 50k every half second if you're standing in it. The fires move as well, so they eventually need to be kited around. \r\n\r\nThe other difference occurs at 30%. When Magmaw is at 30% hp, no more blazing animated skeletons spawn. INtead, Nefarian starts to dish out a shadow ae to random members of the raid until the raid wipes or Magmaw is defeated."},{"id":1337867,"r":18,"n":1,"b":"The add that is summoned every 35 seconds is called [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=49416]Blazing Bone Construct[/url].  \n\nThey actually spawn from a Meteor ([url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=92192]Blazing Inferno[/url]) that lands on the ground.  The area it is going to hit looks very similar to the ground effect used for [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=78006]Pillar of Flame[/url], the ability that spawns Lava Parasites.  You want to move out of the way of the Meteor before it lands, for it deals about 75k fire damage on impact, AND leaves [url=http://wowhead.com/?spell=92198]Ignition[/url] (fire patches) on the ground in a \"S\" type shape, that deal about 55k per second you stand in them (they also move VERY FAST so don't stand anywhere near them).  You will die before you can get out of it, barring a good damage mitigation cooldown.  It is 100% avoidable.  \n\nAt 20% HP the Constructs cast [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=92177]Armageddon[/url], an 8 second cast that when finished, does about 125k fire damage to the raid, effectively a wipe.  So why not just have a tank grab them all and never DPS them, to avoid Armageddon?  They hit extremely hard - after a certain amount you just can't heal through it (if 3 are up at the same time your tank should be using cooldowns until one is dead).  So when a Construct is about to go down, have all DPS hard switch to it, to kill it before the cast finishes.  \n\nBasically, you should avoid all avoidable damage to make this fight easier.  You do that, you're a lot of the way there.  Which means...watch your feet!  Good luck!"}]}{"id":5107,"comments":[{"id":1326496,"r":16,"n":0,"b":"On heroic, Nefarian will periodically mess with one of the abilities used by the Omnotron Defense System.\n\n[b]Magmatron[/b]: The player marked with Acquiring Target will be rooted, meaning everyone else needs to move to avoid the flamethrower.\n\n[b]Electron[/b]: Transforms the lightning rod into an AoE that hits the entire raid, dealing less damage the closer you are to the affected target.\n\n[b]Arcanotron[/b]: Turns a power generator into a bomb, causing it to expand, then detonate in a large explosion that encompasses close to a fourth of the room.\n\n[b]Toxitron[/b]: Warps the raid into the center of an existing chemical cloud, which can potentially cause a wipe if poison bombs are out, and happen to be in or near the cloud at this time.\n\nOn top of this, Arcanotron's Arcane Annihilator does more then twice the amount of damage it does on normal ,meaning it absolutely needs to be interrupted, and the energy for each of the golems decreases around twice as fast as on normal, meaning you'll be switching targets a lot more often, and the abilities used by them can potentially overlap in ways not possible in normal mode."}]}{"id":5108,"comments":[{"id":1249639,"r":33,"n":2,"b":"Does also reward the title :     ..........., Slayer of Stupid, Incompetent and Disappointing Minions"},{"id":1326503,"r":21,"n":0,"b":"Heroic adds an additional phase to the fight that occurs before the red/blue phases in every cycle.\r\n\r\nDuring it, Maloriak will spawn a multitude of Vile Swill adds with high health that need to be kited around the room by the add tank (As they drop ooze puddles almost constantly) and AoE'd down, while Maloriak himself will periodically channel a spell that deals a high amount of shadow damage to his target, and reduces their healing received by 100% for the duration."},{"id":2005498,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"Some background information on this guy: He was once a skilled human alchemist until Nefarian fused him with the corpse of a dragonspawn, making him a Dragonman (\"Dragonkin\")."}]}{"id":5109,"comments":[{"id":1326480,"r":17,"n":1,"b":"The heroic mode adds imps called Obnoxious Fiends that need to be killed immediately, as they'll jump onto the back of a random player, and start chain casting a spell that increases that player's sound if not interrupted.\r\n\r\nNefarian also destroys a random gong in the room whenever you ring one, meaning you only have five to work with in total.\r\n\r\nLastly, all of Atramede's abilities make you gain around 50% more sound then they do on normal (On top of already causing more damage then on normal), which can easily make his Modulation deadly if people mess up even a few times."},{"id":1340406,"r":7,"n":1,"b":"Does modulation damage somehow depend on your sound lever or smthg else? We sometimes takes 80-90k aoe and its wipe us... Usually its much less."}]}{"id":5115,"comments":[{"id":1279596,"r":9,"n":1,"b":"There are 2 major differences on this fight on heroic. The most notable is that Nefarian cancels feud, causing Chimaeron to melee during feuds. In addition, there is a raid wide shadow ae that ticks for 2k every second once you reach p2, making dps quite tight at the end."},{"id":1349288,"r":-6,"n":0,"b":"[url=http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbxvmHKAhmA]25ppl[/url]"},{"id":1393832,"r":10,"n":0,"b":"10-man heroic information/advice (I am a prot pally):\n\n[b]Changes from normal:[/b]\n\n- Chimaeron has 36.2 million health, up from 25.9 million.\n- Nefarian dispels/ends the feud anywhere from 2-5 seconds after the start of the phase. Bile-O-Tron remains down until the next massacre after Feud starts.\n- During phase 2 (last 20%) Nefarian will do a raid wide aura that deals 2000 unresistable shadow damage per second.\n\n[b]General strat information:[/b]\n\nSet up: 2 tanks, 3 healers, 5 dps. One of the dps should be a plate dps with a tank aura/stance up (i.e. dps DK in blood presence, ret pally with RF, etc.)\n\n- The fight is virtually identical for all DPS except the one soaking the Break stacks.\n- We have our dps DK go into blood presence and tank the boss for all of the non-Feud phases (whenever Bile-O-Tron is up). The two tanks (me and a prot warrior) alternate eating the double strikes, based on which tank does not currently have Break stacks from Feud.\n- The number of Massacres Chimaeron does between Feuds has a random element. At the start he can do 2 or 3 massacres before the first Feud, and for every Feud after that he can do 1 or 2. It appears to be completely random how many he does - you can hit the 4th Feud (the one we aim to push him sub-20% on) in as few as 4 massacres (not counting the ones at the end of Feud) or in as many as 7.\n\n- Before 20%, the primary difference is that Chimaeron will need to be tanked during the Feud phases without the Bile-O-Tron up. He will apply Break stacks during this time, so the 2 tanks will need to alternate tanking Chimaeron during the Feud phases. The break debuff lasts 1 minute, and the time from one Feud to the next can never be less than 1 minute, so one tank should always be clear of Feud stacks.\n- Feud can be dispelled very quickly, so healers have to be ready to get the tank healed up quickly after the massacre leading into Feud.\n- Tanks should work out a CD rotation to handle tanking Chimaeron without the Bile-O-Tron up ahead of time. You will need CDs to survive the double attack and his regular melee attacks once you have Break stacks. \n- The tank should NOT stack up with the rest of the raid during the Feud phases - the poison bolt volley damage combined with Chimaeron's hard-hitting melee can instantly gib a tank, even through CDs. 9 people stacked up is still more than enough to split the poison bolt volley damage and survive.\n\n- Before pushing Chimaeron to 20%, the entire raid should be topped off as much as possible to maximize survival from Nefarian's raid-wide AOE. We find that getting everyone above 75% should be sufficient with good DPS.\n- Bile-O-Tron is fairly useless during the last 20% since you will die a second later from Nefarian's AOE after being reduced to 1 HP, so it is fine (and even recommended) to push Chimaeron while the Bile-O-Tron is not up. We find the best strat is to push to 21%, wait for a Feud, top everyone off after the Massacre, then push him before the poison bolt volleys start going out.\n- I am not 100% sure about this, so confirmation would be nice, but from our experience Chimaeron's threat table is not the standard \"highest aggro\" one sub-20%. He seems to go for the highest aggro [i]in melee range[/i], so the best strat is to stack your healers, melee DPS, and tanks all on Chimaeron and have the range stay out. That way your healers die before the ranged DPS. Whenever I tried standing on the other side of the room so he'd have to waste time chasing me (then bubble so he'd waste time running to 2nd threat, cancelaura so he'd run back to me, etc.), he would gib our melee DPS and any healers in melee range before coming to me (despite me being highest on threat), which is why I believe this is the case.\n- If your healers can taunt, it is a good idea to have them do so at some point before pushing Chimaeron sub-20%. That way they will die before the DPS (even the melee) during the burn phase. Holy paladins can heal with RF up for added threat.\n- Save cooldowns such as battle res/soulstone, ankh, etc. for the burn phase.\n\n[b]Prot paladin specific advice:[/b]\n- The big issue I kept having with CD management was that the two big prot paladin CDs (Ardent Defender and GoAK) are 3 minute CDs. Since the time from one Feud to the next can be 1 minute (one massacre) or 1.5 minutes (two massacres) and we aim to push him sub-20% on the 4th Feud (which means I have to tank him twice), the only way those two CDs will be up the second time if I use them the first time I tank him is if he does 2 massacres on both the 3rd and 4th feuds, which will more likely than not fail to occur.\n- To counter this, I worked out a different set of CDs for the first time I tank Chimaeron:\n\n1. Pop the on use on [item=59515] at the start of Feud - this puts me over the 102.4% cap for most of the Feud, which means healers only have to keep me above ~70k (somewhat more with break stacks)\n2. Self BoP + taunt + cancelaura on the Double Strike (this has the added bonus of clearing any Break stacks on you)\n3. DP + Holy Paladin HoSac after the double strike, when you will be taking additional damage due to Break.\n\nThis allows me to have both GoAK and AD up for the 4th one, when we push him sub-20%. This makes a big difference during the burn phase, as I can survive at least 2 more swings from Chimaeron with those CDs up (I use 4-piece tier bonus, so the 50% shield wall lasts through 3 attacks instead of two. Since every 3rd attack is a double attack, this makes a big difference!) The extra 10+ seconds you buy for your DPS can be the difference between a sub-2% wipe and a kill.\n\n- I always HoSac the prot warrior tank on the double strikes whenever he is tanking Chimaeron without the Bile-O-Tron up. Smooths out the damage and serves as an extra safety net.\n\n\n\nHope this helps, and good luck."}]}{"id":5116,"comments":[{"id":1126503,"r":30,"n":4,"b":"Let the games BEGIN!\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n .......again!"},{"id":1127764,"r":6,"n":0,"b":"Title Reward gained from kill on hc mode: [b]Blackwing's Bane[/b]"},{"id":1290679,"r":8,"n":1,"b":"World First in Heroic mode was by Paragon EU-Lightning's Blade, 9 January.\r\nNormal mode World First was by Экзорсус EU-Свежеватель Душ. (Russian?)\r\n\r\nSo far, no one else took Nefarian Heroic down.\r\n\r\nThat's from Wowprogress."},{"id":1683814,"r":7,"n":0,"b":"Easily the hardest heroic mode in the entire meta, Nefarian's extra heroic mode abilities really screw with everyone. He has an addition ability in each of the 3 phases. This strategy only applies to 10 man.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 1[/u]\r\nIn phase 1 and 3, an ability is cast on a random 2 people (not tanks) called Dominion. You cannot move yourself, but are slowly walking to a portal like object. There is a purple beam between you and this portal. This is a mind control-like ability gives you a new action bar with 2 abilities. The first ability breaks it immediately. So what's the point of it then? Well the second ability is a stacking damage buff (a really big one). All DPS want to spam it to stack their buff until they're just about to reach the portal. Then break the ability. Healers want to break it immediately. Players afflicted with dominion become hostile and therefore don't take any damage from Nefarian's electrocutes. These players can also be slowed to prolong the amount of time to spam the buff. If you hit the portal it's an instant death.\r\nOther than that, you want to assign an add tank, not kiter in phase one. The adds move very quickly and will easily rip apart any hunter or mage class that is attempting to kite them. I recommend a warrior or DK. Holy paladins also work well. Have the adds die in one place so that they are easily picked up in phase 3.\r\n    Our group DPSed Onyxia down to 2 million and then switched to Nef and brought him to 40 million (2 electrocutes and almost a third). DoTs brought Ony down to about 600k and Nef down to about 38 million. Finish off Onyxia and then get to pillars. If you get an electrocute at the beginning of phase 2 it's going to be an instant wipe. Trust me.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 2[/u]\r\nThe damage of the lava and the AoE that Nef throws out is significantly higher now. In addition, all 3 adds must die at the same time, because if one dies phase 2 ends, instead of the last one dying. The cast time is now about 3 times shorter, which means very quick interrupts are needed.\r\n   The additional ability in this phase is called Explosive Cinders. It is a debuff put on a random person (only 1 person), which explodes to deal about 50k damage to others within 10 yards and knocks them back, effectively killing them. If you get this debuff, run into the lava after it has about 4 seconds on the duration, and let it explode. SWIM through the lava, do NOT jump. It'll do less damage if you swim. Jumping adds an extra stack each time. Once the ability blows up, get back on the platform and hope that you don't die. One of these abilities will go out right as the phase begins. This one is always the trickiest, and the person who gets it should stay in the lava until it goes off, rather than swimming up to the pillar first. Big heals are required on this target as he/she will have around 10 stacks of the lava. Make sure that this person is far away from the pillar too, not right up against it.\r\n     I recommend two interrupters per pillar. One with a 10 second or less CD interrupt, and one backup. All melee classes work perfectly as your \"less than 10 second\" interrupter, and paladin healers can also do this. Back-up mages are great, as their CD is long, but able to be cast at range. We tended to put our tanks as interrupters (DK and paladin) and have our melee be the backups. Arcane Torrent works as well, bloodelves. We took each of our adds down to 600k health. Then we nuked them. Make sure they're about even before nuking them to death. The first death starts phase 3.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 3[/u]\r\nIf you're lucky, the adds from phase 1 will be in a neat pile and the offtank will have no trouble picking them up. This phase is 1 MILLION% on the offtank who's kiting the adds. I would run them to the outside ring and run them in a large circle around the place. Have a healer who is designated to keep him up. This healer needs to be running around with him. Always be moving, and don't walk backwards. If the adds get touched by fire even once you will be ripped to shreds by them before they can die again. Make sure that the healer uses a CD on the offtank when each electrocute comes out, as it hurts pretty badly. We often had electrocutes kill the offtank resulting in a wipe. If the offtank dies, don't bother brezzing him. It's a wipe. The adds will first kill the offtank healer in 1 shot, then run to the raid, which is through fire, and be unstoppable.\r\n    Dominion is still in effect in phase 3. Use it to your advantage, DPS increase! Arcane mages have 1 million crits with the buff, so it really boosts DPS. Once Nef gets below 10 million, lust it up and blow him up. At that point, he has 2 electrocutes left in him and he will die before the last one goes off (probably). So just kill kill.\r\n     Pick your add tank wisely. If the add tank is bad, it will be a phase 3 wipe EVERY TIME. The add damage is unforgiving if they are allowed to stay alive. \r\n\r\n      Last Notes: Phase 2 is easily the hardest one to heal, and the person who first gets the Explosive Cinders on them often dies. If cinders get on your interrupter, make sure that the backup is ready to do the interrupt. Letting one tick get off on one interrupt will most likely cause a few deaths, and a raid wipe if it's at the beginning of the phase. It just puts healers so far behind. Don't miss your interrupts. Make sure people with Cinders move OUT, and kite adds well in phase 3. That's what really makes this fight possible.\r\n\r\nGood luck :)"},{"id":2095263,"r":-3,"n":0,"b":"Can you get the achievement + the title from 10 man HC?"}]}{"id":5117,"comments":[{"id":1166611,"r":16,"n":0,"b":"The two main differences in the heroic version of the fight are the presence of adds in the Twilight Realm that spam an AoE on the entire raid for as long as they live, and a debuff that is applied to whoever is tanking Valiona/Theralion, that upon reaching five stacks causes them and anyone near them to be warped into the Twilight Realm, meaning the fight now requires two tanks."}]}{"id":5118,"comments":[{"id":1278727,"r":8,"n":1,"b":"[b]Heroic 25-Player Difficulty Strategy[/b]\r\n[i]All of the drakes are active in heroic difficulty. Halfus' HP is also 184.7M[/i]\r\n\r\nSetup recommendation: [b]FIVE[/b] tanks (best geared tank drakes & whelps, worst two alternate between Halfus and the Nether Scion); 2-5 fire mages + warlocks; 2-3 disc priests\r\n\r\nOn the [b]pull[/b], the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=44645]Nether Scion[/url], [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=44797]Time Warden[/url], [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=44641]Orphaned Emerald Whelps[/url], and [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=44650]Storm Rider[/url] should be activated by separate people immediately. (either the tanks or misdirects) This will grant an immediate 200% damage increase to Halfus as well as trivialize every mechanic that makes this encounter deadly. Your better tanks should be holding onto the drakes with your worst two trading off between Halfus and the Nether Scion.\r\n\r\nBecause Halfus is taking 3x the damage, you can trivialize a lot of the tank healing by having your disc priests spec into [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=81749]Atonement[/url] and spam [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=585]Smite[/url] on the boss. Your fire mages will be doing the most AoE damage with [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=44457]Living Bomb[/url] planted on the boss. It's the same with Warlocks and [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=27243]Seed of Corruption[/url]. The whelp pack should die from just these DoTs instead of requiring everyone to throw AoE down.\r\n\r\nThe Storm Rider should be the first to die, followed by the Time Warden. When the Storm Rider is nearly dead, you need to activate the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=44652][/url] to activate the final stack of damage taken by Halfus. You do not have time to kill another drake, and must rotate cooldowns to keep all your tanks alive after 50%. When the Slate Dragon is activated, Halfus will also be stunned periodically making tank damage and interrupting less of a hassle. Once two drakes and the whelps are down, you are only healing 3 tanks (Halfus, Nether Scion, Slate Dragon) instead of 5.\r\n\r\nFor interrupting Shadow Nova, you are inevitably going to get hit by one .5s cast at the start because of the time it takes for the Storm Rider to activate. Anyone who is not a main interrupt on the boss should anticipate this first one coming up and kick it. After that, your main interrupters should be focusing on the boss. It is either two rogues which alternate Kick or an enhancement shaman that has a short enough cooldown on Wind Shear. (The CD on Shadow Nova is about 7-8s) It is imperative that besides the first one absolutely no Shadow Novas go off. After Halfus hits 50%, he will start spamming Furious Roar. Your melee will not be able to interrupt the Shadow Nova in time and need assistance from the mages. Each cast is 1.5, and the resulting stun is 1.5s. When he casts the third stun, mages be ready to blink and spam [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=2139]Counterspell[/url]. If Halfus hits his enrage, you will not be able to interrupt Shadow Novas and must pop any vulnerabilities to squeeze in the remaining amount of time."},{"id":1340085,"r":-7,"n":0,"b":"[url=http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RQr4Ie7bHCs]kill this boss in 25 ppl[/url]"},{"id":1392270,"r":9,"n":0,"b":"10-man heroic information/advice (I am a prot pally):\n\n[b]Changes from normal:[/b]\n\nAll 5 drakes are active. Halfus has 51.5 million health, up from 32.5 million.\n\n[b]General strat information:[/b]\n\nSet up: 3 tanks, 3 healers, 4 dps. This is pretty much standard for this fight on heroic 10m.\n\n- Your tanks need to set up a taunt rotation to make sure the mortal strike stacks do not get out of hand on any one tank. We usually tank swap at 4-5 stacks, and rotate through all 3 tanks until 2-3 dragons are down.\n- Since your tank should not be hit-capped, you should have a DPS with a 10 sec or less CD interrupt taking care of the shadow novas. We have our enhance shaman do it; he puts Halfus on focus, then uses a macro that allows him to interrupt Halfus without losing his current target. The macro looks something like this:\n\n/tar Halfus\n/cast Wind Shear\n/targetlastenemy\n\nIf you use such a macro, make sure you are facing Halfus while DPSing, or else you will get an error when you go for the interrupt and the shadow nova will hit the raid.\n\n- Releasing Nether Scion and Storm Rider on the pull is mandatory. Slate is optional and should be left until last, and we do not even bother releasing him at all.\n- If your tanks can handle 4 drakes (i.e. everything but Slate on the pull) then go for it, but we found releasing 3 at the start made healing more manageable and we still beat the enrage comfortably. We chose to release Time Warden since the damage from the proto-Behemoth's breath, while somewhat heavy, is predictable and not that hard to heal for the first minute or so. We found the fireball barrage damage from not releasing Time Warden was too unpredictable and spiky.\n- Pop bloodlust at the start, and nuke down the first dragon of choice. After killing the first drake (doesn't matter which), we release the whelps, AOE like crazy, then focus down the remaining active dragons and nuke Halfus. \n- Once you get two drakes down, the fight becomes pretty much identical to normal. The hardest part is the first minute, minute and a half. A mage helps quite a bit during the furious roar/shadow nova combo, but we did not have a mage, so we set up a bubble/BoP rotation (i.e. I bubble+interrupt the first, our holy paladin does the second, holy paladin BoPs a DPS for the third, and he should be dead by then.)\n\n\n[b]Prot paladin specific advice:[/b]\n- I usually tank Halfus at the start. I use DP right off the bat, shield wall at 4-5 stacks, BoP+taunt+cancelaura at 12-13 stacks (this clears your MS stacks). This minimizes the need for tank swapping, and our first tank swap usually doesn't occur until after the first dragon dies.\n- Since there will be a gap from the initial pull to the application of Nether Scion's debuff, I usually pull Halfus at max range with AS, then run straight back until he's about to hit me (almost to the back of the room). I turn around and tank him right before can start hitting me with my back turned, and the Nether Scion debuff is usually on by this point. If you try to tank him without the Nether Scion debuff, he will apply stacks very quickly (~1 stack/sec in my estimation) and you will be unhealable very fast. There is a long enough gap from the initial pull to the first shadow nova that you don't have to worry about the travel time of Storm Rider's debuff.\n- I use DG in 2 cases: 1) when the proto behemoth breathes on us before we release the whelps and the raid is a little low on health, and 2) during the furious roars, again if the raid seems a bit low.\n\n\nHope this helps, and good luck."}]}{"id":5119,"comments":[{"id":1299796,"r":-18,"n":0,"b":"2.01 Paragon - world first (25h)"},{"id":1384395,"r":43,"n":0,"b":"This heroic encounter features a few significant changes over its normal counterpart, broken up by each phase.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 1[/u]\r\nFeludius and Ignacious retain all their abilities from normal and do not gain any new abilities, however many of their abilities are boosted. Primarily, letting Hydro Lance fire is very likely to lead to a raid death and Ignacious' shield absorbs significantly more damage.\r\n\r\nThe major change is that the two inactive lords assist their counterparts by tossing debuffs onto raid members. Terrastra will debuff a random non-tank with [spell=92075] and Arion will debuff a random non-tank with [spell=92067]. As the debuffs state, they will pulse and afflict nearby players with secondary debuffs which drastically slow cast/move speed and deal moderate damage over time respectively. The primary debuffs have no duration and can [u]only[/u] be removed by having the two players (one with each type of debuff) stand on top of each other, which causes both debuffs to drop after 1-3 seconds (always watch, lag may be a factor).\r\n\r\nThe goal here is to handle phase 1 normally but also while forced to spread out to avoid too much debuff spreading, which can be trickier than it sounds once you have fire and water bombs everywhere.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 2[/u]\r\nAgain this phase is largely the same except for interference by the two non-active lords. This time, Feludius will summon a frost orb that fixates on a player and chases them, slowly gaining speed in the process. Around the same time Ignacious will mark a target on the ground (very distinct visual) and soon afterwards spawn a flamestrike at that area. The person kiting the frost orb must get the orb to go inside the flamestrike, which will despawn both. Expect to have a frost orb and flamestrike up for about 50% of phase 2 total.\r\n\r\n[u]Phase 3[/u]\r\nThis phase has the fewest changes but is the hardest simply because the challenge was already about burning the Monstrosity down in time, and now with significantly more health and more damage caused from his elemental abilities, killing him before being overwhelmed will require very precise positioning to not chain the lightning. The most marked change is that the ice patches he spawns underneath him grow much more rapidly while he stands in them, which is most noticeable when he channels his Gravity Crush and does not move for the duration. Good luck!"}]}{"id":5120,"comments":[{"id":1158106,"r":31,"n":1,"b":"Defeating Cho'gall on this difficulty causes the floor to collapse, revealing the optional boss, Sinestra."},{"id":1410498,"r":22,"n":1,"b":"There are a few marked changes in this encounter vs. its normal counterpart. I'll do my best to break them down by factors you'll have to deal with individually. First and foremost Cho'gall has significantly more HP than in normal so your raid dps will need to be quite high to defeat this encounter.\r\n\r\nProbably the most important change you'll encounter first is the change to [spell=93366]. Rather than giving Cho'gall a stacking 10% damage buff for 20 seconds increasing every 3 seconds you Worship, it will now give Cho'gall a 5% damage buff that lasts one minute. Since he will cast [spell=93204] at roughly the same rate of every 20 seconds, it becomes crucial to interrupt all mind controls before any stacks are applied as you may quickly become overwhelmed by not being able to drop the Worship stacks.\r\n\r\nThe next major change is the elementals he summons throughout phase 1. Rather than do nothing but get absorbed into his weapon as in normal, they will be attackable for approximately 10 seconds before getting absorbed. It is important to bring them to 1 HP as for every 10% of their health remaining, Cho'gall will do 5% more damage from their effect (direct fire damage to tank from fire elemental, raid shadow pulse from shadow elemental). \r\n\r\nThere are two corrupted adherents spawning at a time in 25-heroic (still only one in 10-heroic),  but their increased health and that of the spawned blood means you will need to be dropping these in roughly the same location as to be able to destroy the bloods as efficiently as possible. If you're meeting the DPS requirement you should be pushing phase 2 just before or after the 5th set of adherents spawns.\r\n\r\nPhase 2 is primarily made more difficult by the increased health to burn through while the entire raids corruption bar slowly ticks upward. However, to further complicate matters, [npc=50265]s will spawn roughly every 25-30 seconds close to Cho'gall. These cannot be effectively killed and the entire raid must be careful to avoid them, as while they only melee they hit for significant damage.\r\n\r\nAt 2% Cho'gall will begin staggering toward the trapdoor in the middle of the room. He will only die when he has reached it, falling on it and causing it to break. You can avoid a low-% wipe by keeping him close to the trapdoor when he reaches 5% or so, as you will not need to wait for him to move and ending the fight that much earlier. His body can be located for looting below in the Twilight Caverns."},{"id":1701696,"r":-5,"n":0,"b":"If you have a choice, try finding a paladin tank for this, Avenger's Shield is very handy for interrupting the Worship."},{"id":6389605,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"We managed to finish the glory today. (Heroic Cho'gall is bugged right now...)\r\n\r\nI came with friend in party, we pulled boss with taunt to the middle of the room (killed all the adds before pull), then after few seconds nuked him to 0%, he then revived to full HP and bugged, we waited like 10-15s, my friend who taunted and pulled the boss used shadowmeld, then moved a little a bit and then hearthstoned. After he disappeared I waited for few seconds, boss got into the middle, died and I got the achievement. Worked twice in the row."},{"id":6404698,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"August 2026.  Our guild wanted to complete the Cataclysm Raider Guild Achievement, and Cho'gall was our last one, but we haven't been able to get it due to the glitch.  Tonight, though, we were prepared:  Everyone on a hunter or a rogue or a night elf, everyone naked (cuz why not?) and ready to go.  We killed the left and right mobs - check!  We pulled Cho'gall into the middle of the room - check!  Damaged him and prepared for the glitch - everyone's fingers hovering nervously over their shadowmeld/vanish/feign death spells - we started the 10 second countdown as recommended - when **BOOM**!   Achieve complete.  No glitch.  No problem.  No idea why.  I like to think it's because we're good people, and karma served some justice, but maybe, just maybe....  the glitch has been fixed?  I hope it is easily achieved for everyone else who tries it now, too."}]}{"id":5121,"comments":[{"id":1127766,"r":36,"n":1,"b":"Title Reward gained from kill on hc mode: [b]Dragonslayer[/b]"},{"id":1150656,"r":80,"n":6,"b":"Trivia: Sinestra was (in life) one of the few, if not the only one, mates of Deathwing who could bear the heat emanating from his body (But not without a price, the scars of their mating never healed). [i](I cannot heal him so I have to kill the boss before he dies, which at lvl 110 is easy.)[/i]\r\n\r\nAfter some RP destroy the eggs and then her. Took less than 2 min total."},{"id":2527637,"r":50,"n":3,"b":"At 110, this event is more likely to reset than you are to die. This is the method I used:\r\n1. Attack her until the shield spawns\r\n2. Get in the shield\r\n3. Kill the whelps etc as they come\r\n4. Attack her to reduce her mana pool shield until the yellow text in chat appears: \"The barrier protecting the Pulsing Twilight Eggs dissipates as Sinestra harnesses their power!\" (there is no audible cue for this)\r\n5. DPS her down fast"}]}{"id":5122,"comments":[{"id":1332341,"r":23,"n":2,"b":"I made an instructional for Ravenous Creeper kiting if any DK is having trouble with this.  \r\n\r\nhttp://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WTLvb09x-_I"},{"id":1380268,"r":-2,"n":0,"b":"You made it look easy as pie, very nice. But might i suggest turning overlapping plates on? xD"},{"id":1384761,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"made a video from rosh POV as a melee class\r\n\r\nhttp://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXzahUORcb4"},{"id":1422913,"r":15,"n":0,"b":"Major differences between normal and hard:\r\n\r\nRohash's Wind Blast is now lethal, you can not survive being hit by it in. In addition it moves much faster and has a larger radisu.\r\nRohash now occasionally puts up a Wind Shield, everyone on the platform takes 30k damage per tick until it gets destroyed.\r\nRohash puts a stacking debuff on the target he is attacking, meaning target swapping is necessary\r\n\r\nNezir is mostly the same, but the damage he does is much more threatening. 5+ stacks of the debuff can become lethal. Frost patches will slow and root you in a few seconds now. His AoE during ultimate is also more deadly so everyone needs to stack up and get AoE heals + barrier.\r\n\r\nAnshal's major difference is that the adds are extremely deadly, their AoE pulse will instantly kill you. Thus they need to be kited for the entire fight. A frost DK is ideal, with the help from Mages' ring of frost each time they come up. The videos above provide some good instruction."},{"id":2020410,"r":18,"n":1,"b":"Not too hard to solo in 6.0.2, but you have to kill them in the right order:\r\n[ol][li]Anshal first, so you don't have 100% healing debuff ([spell=85576]) when you're not on his platform.[/li]\r\n[li]As caster, Nezir second, so you don't have 500% haste debuff when you're not on his platform.[/li][/ol]\r\nMake sure to stay on each platform until the boss is dead. If you jump away and let your DoTs finish him off, you will get the boss's debuff as you fly away, and you may not lose it when it dies."},{"id":2368526,"r":7,"n":0,"b":"I love the no loot bug that's been happening for years and still isn't fixed, with no fix or hope in sight ever."}]}{"id":5123,"comments":[{"id":1385346,"r":22,"n":0,"b":"[b][u]Differences in Heroic:[/u][/b]\n\n1) [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=93260]Ice Storm[/url] can now go into melee range and will subsequently leave ice patches that need to be avoided by melee DPS and tanks.\n\n2) [url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=93257]Lightning Strike[/url] now lasts approximately 25 seconds instead of being instant, it will deal its damage every second to those caught within its cone.\n\n3) The AoE pulse that [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=47175]Stormlings[/url] have increases nature damage taken by targets hit by its effect by 25% for 2 seconds. This effect stacks and compounded with the actual damage from the AoE pulse can quickly kill anyone nearby."},{"id":2328874,"r":3,"n":0,"b":"To all the people having trouble with this achievement...just do slow dps, you mustn't burst until he throws you up in the air"}]}

> {"id":4852,"comments":[{"id":1072735,"r":42,"n":2,"b":"A reference to the popular video game Double Dragon."},{"id":1333831,"r":63,"n":2,"b":"[quote]There also seems to be only one fiend present for each phase transition, meaning you'll need to enter the twilight realm six times to get enough for the achievement.[/quote]\r\n\r\nThis is untrue.\r\n\r\nThey spawn at intervals of roughly 10-15 seconds.\r\n\r\nThis achievement is semi RNG, depending on how many people you send into the twilight realm.\r\nIt is possible to get all six in about a minute in the realm. The fiend spawn in random locations... and run what seems to be 25-30 yards before despawning. The trick is to spot them asap, slow them, then kill them. Problem being the random locations. They can spawn anywhere. etc, center of the room, near either of the bosses starting points. The room is 180y x 60y. In theory for 10 man, if you have 3 people stationed in the center line longways, preferably ranged slowers on the top stairs & a good rogue/dk stationed in the center, 1 center and 2 on the top of the steps spaming the macro\r\n\r\n[code]/tar twilight fiend[/code]\r\n\r\nyou shouldn't have a problem meeting the criteria in 2 Dazziling destruction phases. \r\nSome reason, people get insta jibbed in the DEEP BREATH, might be a timing thing of running in and out quickly, needs more testing.\r\n\r\nYou will accumulate 12 stacks by the time 3 fiends spawn. Cloak, bubble, non specific despell ablities are your best friend in increasing your kill counter. Also, avoid the \"real\" realm AoE abilites from the boss at all costs. 10+% per stack shadow damage + unavoidable AoE + Boss abilites + %^&*ing orbs = oh @#$%.\r\n\r\nIn short, As long as you have enough people covering most of the ground, killing 6 fiends shouldn't be a problem."},{"id":2072364,"r":313,"n":7,"b":"[b]Idiots guide for [achievement=4852] in 6.0 (Healing Class Edition)\r\n[/b]\r\n1. Agro [npc=45992] [i](but don't burn her down)[/i]\r\n2. She casts [spell=86788] twice. Soak it up and top up your health.\r\n3. [npc=45993] will then cast [spell=86408].\r\n4. Stand in the shadow-pool caused by [spell=86408]. This will take you into the shadow realm.\r\n5. Target [npc=49864]s as they appear and kill them. You need 6 for the achievement.\r\n6. The achievement should pop when you kill the sixth [npc=49864] if you have downed the boss on a previous run."},{"id":2079083,"r":40,"n":2,"b":"As an L100 this was super easy.  One note:  You can wait inside until you get all 6 kills.  Don't leave after 3."},{"id":2478995,"r":22,"n":1,"b":"I've tried this achievement and failed at 110. Going into the twilight realm, I started shooting the ads and noticed the boss health declining, even though I was single targeting.\r\n\r\nAfter checking the Combat Log, it turns out the [item=140798] trinket from NH was damaging the bosses with Carrion Swarm. Turns out the trinkets works like Thorns and not how it is meant to. Beware of trinkets, killing the bosses"},{"id":3210186,"r":6,"n":0,"b":"I just got this achieve (last one for Glory of the Cataclysm Raider AND the Drake of the East Wind!) using my lvl 120 Balance Druid after failing on 2 other characters.
