[spell=89696] [spell=90453] [spell=90458] [spell=90610] [spell=90611] [spell=91766]"},{"id":1242928,"r":12,"n":1,"b":"The story of Pyramond and Theleste (as we know it from the descriptions of the artifacts) maybe references to a number of different romantic tragedies. I can identify two, but I'm confident the others will also be references to plays. Chest of Tiny Glass Animals - [b]Glass Menagerie[/b] Cracked Crystal Vial - [b]Romeo and Juliette[/b] Cloak Clasp with Antlers Hairpin of Silver and Malachite Delicate Music Box Silver Scroll Case"},{"id":1254716,"r":74,"n":3,"b":"The achievement's name is likely a reference to three-act plays as a general subject. The names \"Pyramond and Theleste\" are likely references to Pyramus and Thisbe, two characters from Ovid's Metamorphoses, in a story very similar to most romantic tragedies, that has been noted to be the source of Shakespeare's more widely known Romeo and Juliet. Indeed, the items necessary for the achievement do reference these dramas, as well as others. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=63407]Cloak Clasp with Antlers[/url] is a reference to Pyramus and Thisbe itself, as Pyramus sees Thisbe's cloak on the ground, torn to shreds by the nearby lion, and mistakenly interprets it as a sign of her death. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64381]Cracked Crystal Vial[/url] is a reference to Romeo and Juliet, specifically the vial of poison that Romeo purchased from an Apothecary for the purpose of suicide should he find Juliet dead. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64356]Hairpin of Silver and Malachite[/url] is a reference to the Chinese folktale of Niu Lang and Zhi Nu. The Hairpin in the tale was one of gold, and it was used by the Queen Mother to make a large river appear between the lovers. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64379]Chest of Tiny Glass Animals[/url] is a reference to The Glass Menagerie, a memory play. The glass animals are prized possessions of Laura, one of the four major players in the drama. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64357]Delicate Music Box[/url] is hard to place as a reference; it is likely not a reference to a specific work, but rather to the general romantic nature of Music Boxes. The [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64648]Silver Scroll Case[/url] is much harder to place. I have found no likely reference as of writing."},{"id":1262580,"r":-3,"n":0,"b":"I noticed ingame the names of the character, obvious plays of Pyramus and Thisbe (noted in Shakespeare's \"A Mid-summers Night Dream.\")"},{"id":1263154,"r":134,"n":18,"b":"Here are the flavor texts of each one of the six artifacts required for this achievement. For quick reference. As well as to make it easier for readers to figure out the story of Pyramond and Theleste. [ul] [li][quote=\"Delicate Music Box\"]This box is of sandalwood with a tiny clockwork elf and nightsaber within. Although the winding mechanism is no longer functional, you can imagine the two would dance together while music played. Engraved on the bottom: 'To my dearest Theleste.'[/quote] Not a terrible lot one can extract from this one. Pyramond loved Theleste and gave her this music box as a gift.[/li] [li][quote=\"Cloak Clasp with Antlers\"]This clasp is fashioned of lacquered wood carved to resemble stag antlers. On the reverse is engraved the name 'Pyramond' in Darnassian.[/quote] So Pyramond owned this. One could claim the antlers were some symbol associated with him - perhaps he was a druid? Or a noble?[/li] [li][quote=\"Hairpin of Silver and Malachite\"]Engraved beneath the setting for the precious stone are the words 'To Theleste, on her twenty-fourth birth year.'[/quote] Another one of Pyramond's gifts, likely. It could be from her parents, but the precious stone makes that option seem unlikely. Also, the fact that this was a gift for Theleste's 24th birthday suggests that she was probably not an elf - she would have been to young for romance at that age. Human, maybe? We don't know how old the artifacts are, but if they were from the pre-Sundering times, that would be almost impossible, as night elves and humans did not interact. Could be an elf, after all...[/li] [li][quote=\"Chest of Tiny Glass Animals\"]Remarkably, you managed to find an entire menagerie of these elven glass animals in their original storage container. While some of the animals have understandably suffered cracks and chips, it is clear that the head of the stag has been deliberately severed. The initial 'T' is carved on the bottom of the chest.[/quote] This one is puzzling. It looks like the chest belonged to Teleste, as indicated by the initial 'T'. The head of the stag being deliberately severed vaguely suggests strong negative emotion - hatred or sadness/despair. Since we know the chest is related to the story between her and Pyramond, we could assume that the stag is another symbol for Pyramond - after all his cloak pin had antlers on it. Both noble and a druid are equally likely vocations for Pyramond.[/li] [li][quote=\"Cracked Crystal Vial\"]A note in rich vellum is tied to the bottle. 'Dearest P, now that I know we can never be together, it is my wish to drink this draught of spider venom. If this note finds you, my hope is that you might do the same. May Elune watch over our souls.'[/quote] The \"dearest P\" must be Pyramond. For some reason Theleste decided that the two can't be together and pulled a Juliet on him. Her call to Elune suggests that either she was an elf, or her love for Pyramond made her believe in the moon goddess.[/li] [li][quote=\"Silver Scroll Case\"]While this elven scroll case is graced with much ornamentation, it is the message inside, written in Darnassian, that is of the most interest: 'Pyramond, under no circumstances are you to spend time with that tavern wench. Your mother and I forbid it. She is far beneath your station.'[/quote] This must be from Pyramond's father. The language of choice suggests that they were all elves, and there is a likelihood that Pyramond's family was noble as well. I can't imagine an elf being a \"tavern wench\", but apparently Theleste was considered one by Pyramond's parents. Maybe she was a human after all?[/li] [/ul] There are many holes in the story, but it looks like Pyramond was a young noble, perhaps the heir in his house. His family's crest was a stag - or antlers, at least. At some point of time he fell in love with Teleste - a human or an elf girl; young, perhaps working as a waitress in a tavern - or whatever equivalent they had at the time. The two loved each other, but Pyramond's parents found out about the relationship and forbid their son to see his love. Theleste learned that somehow, could overcome the pain, and drank a vial of spider poison, ending her life. She left a note for Pyramond, asking him to do the same so that they could be together in the afterlife. Sometime before she committed the suicide, she - in a fit of sadness or rage - ripped the head off the glass stag, presumably given to her by Pyramond."},{"id":1308034,"r":-4,"n":0,"b":"Praise for ArgentSun! I love the way you analysed these artifacts. They feel more real to me. And so do P and T. This is what makes this profession great!"},{"id":1311003,"r":10,"n":0,"b":"[quote]Another one of Pyramond's gifts, likely. It could be from her parents, but the precious stone makes that option seem unlikely. Also, the fact that this was a gift for Theleste's 24th birthday suggests that she was probably not an elf - she would have been to young for romance at that age. Human, maybe? We don't know how old the artifacts are, but if they were from the pre-Sundering times, that would be almost impossible, as night elves and humans did not interact. Could be an elf, after all...[/quote] It's quite possible that the engraving is not referring to Theleste's age, but some other event celebrating a different measure of age. Since Night Elves aren't adults until they are over 100 years old, and could live for millennia even before Nordrassil prevented them from dying of age, it would make sense that \"birth-year\" could refer to something different and less frequent than an annual birth-date."},{"id":1353264,"r":12,"n":0,"b":"Nicely thought out Argent Sun - but some things I thought up and would like to argue with you: Indeed i think the story is very Romeo and Juliet - the hairpin obviously implies they were young, but probably not [i]that[/i] young during the time of the tragedy. Night Elf lifespan has been implied to be around a few thousand years even without their immortality, so a twenty-four year-old is at least society wise, almost an infant. The severed head of the stag translates in to my mind as the \"head of the family\", it would imply she (Theleste) was mad at Pyramond's father, not Pyramond. Maybe enraged she wanted him dead. Also what you said about the stag in general, it's likely Pyramond was one of the Highborne, and Highborne generally weren't druids but mages, as they dabbled in the arcane magics in general. However, I think even the highborne did to some degree revere [url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Malorne]Malorne[/url], Elune and other night elf deities, therefore they likely would pick something like an antler, or stag, or many other nature related things to be adorned in their house crest. The cloak clasp is just clothing ornamentation, but could obviously be themed after the noble house's crest. Many other night elf archaeology items paint Highborne as extremely vain people with highly ornamented and stylized anything from a comb to a glaive so it shouldn't be that far fetched. Theleste likely was just your average night elf (therefore far beneath Pyramond's station, son of a noble/highborne), and likely believed in Elune's guidance like many others of her kind. I'm pretty certain Theleste was not a human, or of any other race, since aside from Tauren they were the only mention-worthy humanoid races (as I highly doubt neither of them was a Quilboar, Furbolg or a Centaur) in Kalimdor until just mere ten-fifteen years ago, I think also the condition of the music box & glass animals imply the items are far older than a mere decade or two. Aside from these thigns I agree with you, they likely were truly in love, but the world was against them. The story plays out very much like the story of Romeo and Juliet, as many people have noted."},{"id":1370390,"r":-4,"n":0,"b":"It's a trap!"},{"id":1422226,"r":1,"n":1,"b":"Some here seem to be of the opinion that this is a story of forbidden love. However, the message inside the silver scroll case clearly indicates (imho) otherwise; \"Pyramond, under no circumstances are you to spend time with that tavern wench. Your mother and I forbid it. She is far beneath your station\" Here, Pyramond's mother is siding with Theleste. The story is that Pyramond's and Theleste's family have groomed the to young elves for an arranged marriage. Pyramond's gifts to theleste are ones of affection, but hardly of passionate love. However, Pyramond has lost his heart to a young woman who serves in a Tavern, much to the dismay of both Theleste and Pyramond's mother. Theleste, in her rage in finally understanding that she has lost her love, severs the head of the stag representing her love. She then kills herself. It is her hope that Pyramond will do the same, perhaps in the vain hope that they may be together in death or simply for spite."},{"id":1482522,"r":-1,"n":0,"b":"[quote]Some here seem to be of the opinion that this is a story of forbidden love. However, the message inside the silver scroll case clearly indicates (imho) otherwise; \"Pyramond, under no circumstances are you to spend time with that tavern wench. Your mother and I forbid it. She is far beneath your station\" Here, Pyramond's mother is siding with Theleste. The story is that Pyramond's and Theleste's family have groomed the to young elves for an arranged marriage. Pyramond's gifts to theleste are ones of affection, but hardly of passionate love. However, Pyramond has lost his heart to a young woman who serves in a Tavern, much to the dismay of both Theleste and Pyramond's mother. Theleste, in her rage in finally understanding that she has lost her love, severs the head of the stag representing her love. She then kills herself. It is her hope that Pyramond will do the same, perhaps in the vain hope that they may be together in death or simply for spite.[/quote] I find your theory interesting, but if true, would portray Theleste as a vain, superior Noble woman. And, since there is only 3 people directly mentioned within the artifact's descriptions, the 3 being Pyramond, Theleste and Pyramond's mother, this theory is only speculation seeing as there is no real evidence of a 4th character. In fact, the Silver Scroll Case's message would dispute Theleste as being so vain considering that she is asking Pyramond to join her in death. But, to modify your theory, maybe there is a 4th character and instead of Theleste being the vain noblewoman to be married to Pyramond, its the 4th, unmentioned woman who is the arranged bride to be. The writer of the message in the case is the arranged bride telling Pyramond to break it off with Theleste. If you arrange the pieces, the letter could be the turning point in the story if Pyramond chooses his parents wishes over his feeling for Theleste. This could explain why the stag in the Chest of Tiny Glass Animals has had its head severed. Displaying the pain and anger she felt for being rejected. If true, this would place the Cracked Crystal Vial as the last piece in the story."},{"id":1795821,"r":-2,"n":0,"b":"I think you all are making a key error in your assumption about Theleste's age. The hairpin clearly says \"birth YEAR.\" This is not just \"old-timey, RP fancy-talk\" for \"birthday,\" but an indication of the night elf system of keeping track of age given their unusually long lifespans (either immortal, or several thousand years). The use of birth \"years\" indicates a stellar or lunar cycle (like the Zodiac) wherein a particular year would recur within every cycle. Not knowing the length/span of the cycle, Theleste can be assumed to be anywhere from ~100 years old to several hundred years old (which, to an immortal race would still be considered relative adolescence)...but she most certainly is NOT only 24 solar years old."}]},{"a":5192,"c":[{"id":1124261,"r":90,"n":4,"b":"All four of the artifacts are common tier items from the Orc tier in archaeology. It says he had a short reign over the Tol'vir, but nothing indicative that he was young."},{"id":1552824,"r":6,"n":0,"b":"If you go through and read the completed flavor texts of the listed artifacts, a somewhat clear story arises: 1) Ninjter was predicted to be a great ruler of the Tol'vir, bringing a new golden age to the land of Uldum. 2) Much fanfare proceded his rise, with great ornaments and plans drawn up for use during his rule. 3) Against his fate, he somehow died before all those plans could be implemented.. Was it plague, that had ravished the land? Murder, by a jealous rival for the throne? Suicide, for fear of never living up to the immense expectaions upon him? We don't know, and probably never will. He apparently was still greatly loved by the time of his death, if the Alchemy recipe found in one of his Canopic Jars means what I think it means. That, or he himself was an excellent alchemist in his short time."},{"id":1555289,"r":32,"n":1,"b":"Putting together the links and the information for the complete story. This is my guess at the chronological order: [ul] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=91780]Soapstone Scarab Necklace[/url] [quote]'Presented to Emperor Ninjter on the day he assumed the throne. We expect only greatness in his reign.'[/quote] Starts the story. There is no mention of his age, but of course the achieve is \"The BOY Who Would Be King\", a classical reference to the Kipling story \"The MAN Who Would Be King\". It would be nice to have had an arch reference to his age. Either way, obviously great things were expected of him.[/li] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=91779]Cat Statue with Emerald Eyes[/url] [quote]This small clay cat displays a lifelike pose and expression. On the underside is engraved, 'In memory of Chalyx, beloved pet of Emperor Ninjter.'[/quote] My first thought was, well, maybe this is a sign of his age, but then about .0000001 second later, I remembered how much Egyptians revered cats. This gives us a look at him as a person, per se, but nothing historical. /sigh [/li] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=91792]Sketch of a Desert Palace[/url] [quote]These are architectural plans, though the architect apparently dreamed on a very big scale. You are unaware of any structure resembling this palace in modern Uldum, so it is likely the palace was never built. 'Commissioned for Emperor Ninjter.'[/quote] With such an excellent outlook, it seems the young Emperor, or his advisors, set to work plotting a palace that would outshine all others. It was never built. Perhaps this was simply because his reign was so brief, but I kind of thing the next find is a clue....[/li] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=64655]Tiny Oasis Mosaic[/url] [quote]This small piece of artwork has been pieced together from shattered clay tiles colored in brilliant turquoise, green and sand. 'Our hopes and prayers are to Emperor Ninjter, that he may end the famine and restore glory to the Ramkahen!'[/quote] Famine struck. It's possible that the previous architectural creation was still at work (kind of a \"let them eat cake,\" \"Nero fiddled while Rome burned\" kind of thing), but either way, the people were obviously concerned. Rulers can only do so much with famine, especially if they lack sufficient stores, so I think young Ninjter may have attempted another method of finding food...war.[/li] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=91785]Engraved Scimitar Hilt[/url] [quote]This scimitar appears more ornamental than functional. Its blade ends after only a few inches, but it does not appear to have seen much use in combat. Carved in loops of script around the pommel and down the hilt can be read the words 'May Emperor Ninjter lead us to victory! Kadesh! Osadi! Satekh!'[/quote] In an attempt to either distract the masses or to find food when his kingdom was lacking, it seems Emperor Ninjter may have taken to war. Whether he was expected to lead the troops into battle personally or remain a figurehead is something we lack information on, but if he did, in fact, attempt to lead troops while still young and untried, the result may well have been....[/li] [li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/spell=91790]Canopic Jar[/url] [quote]This jar contains the petrified organs of Emperor Ninjter. He apparently died only a few years into what was hoped would be a glorious reign.[/quote] A short reign. [/li][/ul] Of course, this is just supposition. The war could be unlinked to the famine; he could have died for his \"let them eat cake\", build my grand palace on the backs of the starving poor. But, I like the idea of a connection (especially since this isn't random life but a predetermined Blizzard plan). [i]Inspired by [url=http://www.wowhead.com/user=ArgentSun]ArgentSun[/url]'s [url=http://www.wowhead.com/achievement=5191#comments:id=1263154]archeological explanation[/url] of [url=http://www.wowhead.com/achievement=5191]Tragedy in Three Acts[/url][/i]"},{"id":6460709,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"As someone who started WoW. Am I right looking for that in Cataclysm Addon then?"}]},{"a":5511,"c":[{"id":1131658,"r":71,"n":1,"b":"Of course it's always in the last place you look, you wouldn't keep looking after you found it!"},{"id":1132661,"r":85,"n":8,"b":"Each of the races are different tiers in the new profession archaeology. [/b]You don't get rares from regular solves which means you're solving 25 for a single rare. Since bad luck protection exists, you could've got 2-3 rares from another race since generally you will see a new rare in under 10 solves.[/li] [li]Save fragments (and therefore time) by [b]only solving with keystones if possible[/b]. Prioritise the races you can afford the keystones for; some rares are still very popular due to the items from their rare solves (e.g. Zin'Rokh from trolls) whilst others are very cheap. There are enough rares to get the achievement without spending a fortune. Good luck."},{"id":1212593,"r":4,"n":0,"b":"It is always three lots of artifacts per site."},{"id":1213706,"r":0,"n":1,"b":"No one has the same dig sites"},{"id":1215602,"r":6,"n":1,"b":"At three fragments apiece with no keystones usually available on starter items, I advise early archaeologists to use the Survey skill-up levels alone until 100, you can then create a few items for 5 points apiece rather than wasting those 20 or so extra points on what'd you'd be doing anyway."},{"id":1371702,"r":3,"n":0,"b":"I'm kind of confused on this... This is the first achievements in maxing out your profession, and something I would do is continue digging but don't actually \"solve\" any of the pieces until you're close to max artifacts, or after you've trained it again (if you're too close to hitting the end). - [url=http://thewowexp.wordpress.com/]TheWoWExp[/url]"}]},{"a":4919,"c":[{"id":1756818,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"This is the second achievement in the long run of getting maxed out in this profession. While many people may go back and forth throughout Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, I preferred to stay on the side of Eastern Kingdoms from now and up to the last skill point (for those who are curious--I like getting my achievements in all one spot first before moving elsewhere, else my ADD mind can't keep up with myself). At this point you might notice that it does take a little while to level up your Archaeology quickly, what with having to fly from one place to another (at least, I hope you're flying and not running everywhere!), but it pays off with unique pets, mounts, and items you get. - [url=http://thewowexp.wordpress.com/]TheWoWExp[/url]"}]},{"a":4920,"c":[{"id":1248769,"r":8,"n":0,"b":"Got this far? Your doing well. Not the funnest skill in WoW."},{"id":1756839,"r":2,"n":0,"b":"Even if you're not liking leveling this profession as much as the others, you've had to have gotten at least some nifty things from it so far, right? Sometimes even items that offer a special effect may be beneficial in other areas of WoW, such as [item=64358] for PvP uses. If you've lacked anything grand, just remember the junk items you get do sell for gold. In any case, grats on making almost-but-not-quite halfway to the end of this profession. At level 300, you're able to start finding artifacts in Outland--you can set your [item=6948] to Shattrath if you'll be here for a while. - [url=http://thewowexp.wordpress.com/]TheWoWExp[/url]"}]},{"a":4921,"c":[{"id":1225338,"r":3,"n":0,"b":"Some facts about Archaeology 1. Artifacts proccs (as i call them) are random, some ppl make Fossil Raptor at 100 skill some ppl at 450(ye im talking about myself :D) 7. Fossiled Minipet is cute 8. Artifacts cannot be inside buildings(never had inside tho) but can be in destroyed houses, ruins etc etc. 9. Survey gives xp for each looting, 80 lvl ~ 5k; 81~7k, 82~10k, 83~12k, 84~15k (for me + guild perk 5%) 10. I bet u wanna get super rare items, and happy diggin, haunting, and yes good luck. If you do travel to Northrend, and you plan on staying there for a while, you can get away with setting your [item=6948] to Dalaran. That way if you're far off from the next dig site, hearthing to Dal will at least get you somewhat closer. - [url=http://thewowexp.wordpress.com/]TheWoWExp[/url]"}]},{"a":4922,"c":[{"id":1756916,"r":1,"n":0,"b":"You've reached 450; no time to put down your shovel. At 450, you can start digging up artifacts in [zone=5034] for the Tol'vir race and learn their lore. As a tip, while Archaeology isn't the greatest in getting gold like the other professions out there, you can both sell the junk you acquire for a pretty nice sum (sometimes up to 200g for one piece of junk), and keep the keystones you may find along your digging career. While these will help you in solving your archaeology pieces, they may also help others who don't like digging constantly. Sell them on the AH for a bit of extra cash. - [url=https://thewowexp.com]TheWoWExp[/url]"}]},{"a":4923,"c":[{"id":1196513,"r":7,"n":3,"b":"OK... had to do some looking up: Archaeology: Meant to be used as a pass time Loot: Practically everything. A new hearth, new mounts, new pets, BoA weapons that are ONLY lv 85 (no scaling), and more. How it works: Go to your map. Should show you some locations, which vary on your level (ex., a lv 20 won't be sent to Tanaris). Click on that location (ex, Tanaris). That will show you a red-shaded area, where there can be artifacts... but the regions can be HUGE. Go there and use \"Survey\". A little telescope and light (looks Gnomish) will spawn. It points in a direction--that's where you have to follow. The light's an indicator. Red=you have a loooooong way buddy. Yellow=you're getting there. Green=close--about 40ish yards. NOTE: People have different spots, so there's no competition. Once you get within like 5 yards and use Survey, a fragment comes up, and you can loot it. It's only remaining purpose is to now drain time, interest and raise annoyance. What other profession has that?"},{"id":1310199,"r":12,"n":1,"b":"Commons will not repeat unless: [ul] [li]You have gotten every common for that race, OR[/li] [li]Your skill is not high enough to begin progress on a common item you have not yet made. (450 skill unlocks everything)[/li] [/ul] As for rares, you only make them once each. A rare never repeats. You are not guaranteed to get a rare, even if you have completed all commons for that race. Should you get a rare, however, it's guaranteed to not be a rare you've already done (as they can each only be done once.) So what does this really mean? If you start to make a common item that you've already made before, and your skill is 450 or higher, then you're done with that race, as far as this achievement is concerned. You may still have rares to do in that race, but you're done with the common items and can move on to a different race, if this achievement is what you're working on."},{"id":1319841,"r":-3,"n":0,"b":"Regarding Thortok2000 post. You can obtain them from one of dailies in capital cities (1-2 tokens/day), one of daily quests from Dalaran cooking (1-2 tokens/day) and rarely from Dalaran fishing daily (from which quest item can be mailed, traded or auctioned, 5 tokens, multiple items can be used multiple times a day). Quests from classic capitals which yield 2 Epicurean's Award tokens: [quest=26177] / [quest=29353] / [quest=29318] for the Alliance, [quest=29364] / [quest=26220] / [quest=29334] for the Horde. Quest from Dalaran that yields 3 tokens (2 for quest + 1 from bag): [quest=13107] for both factions. Quest item from Dalaran fishing: [item=49667] for both factions. You can complete fishing quest on alts and mail this quest item reward to your cooking main. Recommended fishing skill of around 350 for those dailies. If you manage to get 5 tokens per day (2 from any classic capital, 3 from Dalaran), it'll take 19 days to acquire required 91 tokens. Keep in mind that every [item=49667] will shorten this time by 1 day, so it is worth farming/looking for! Since this achievement requires 30 different cooked meals, there are two ways to acquire additional recipe(s): - two recipes ([spell=88015], [spell=88006]) are taught by a huge number of cooking trainers, - two recipes ([item=62800], [item=62799]) can be bought from guild vendors (for 150g each) after your guild earns achievements (respectively [achievement=5036] and [achievement=5467]). In order to cook all those recipes, you'll need tons of ingredients from fishing, killing mobs or vendor. know..."}][{"id":1660687,"r":16,"n":0,"b":"Horde, level 85 with 525 Cooking, having earned the title of Chef, my [b]Iron Chef progress was 160/200 known recipes[/b] with only 7 recipes known for Cataclysmic Gourmet (I had both Guild recipes and Thistle Tea recipe, rogue only). I have picked up a handful (probably less than 10) recipes that were reputation or vendor or location drop specific in my time of questing and running raids/dungeons. I went through the recipes listed on WoWhead and ignored those purchasable for cooking commendations and these are the recipes I was missing (they are quest/drops, vendor specific, quest specific, trainer specific or opposite faction).[b] NOTE: None of the recipes I have listed require cooking daily commendations to purchase.[/b] This is not a full list of all recipes exclusive to vendors, however this helped me boost closer to Iron Chef with recipes purchased without daily cooking commendations from the ones that I had not learned at this point. [u] [b]These are only obtainable by Alliance:[/b][/u] [item=6329 domain=www] - Loch Frenzy Delight - Loch Modan at 40, 39 from Khara Deepwater [item=5528 domain=www] - Clam Chowder - Westfall at 36, 90 from Kriggon Talsone [item=2699 domain=www] - Redridge Goulash - Stormwind at 76,53 from Kendor Kabonka [item=3680 domain=www] - Murloc Fin Soup - Stormwind at 76,53 from Kendor Kabonka [item=2697 domain=www] - Goretusk Liver Pie - Stormwind at 76,53 from Kendor Kabonka [item=3681 domain=www] - Crockolisk Gumbo - Stormwind at 76,53 from Kendor Kabonka [item=3678 domain=www] - Crockolisk Steak - Stormwind at 76,53 from Kendor Kabonka [item=2701 domain=www] - Seasoned Wolf Kabob (Quest) [item=27686 domain=www] - Roasted Moongraze Tenderloin (Quest) [item=3683 domain=www] - Gooey Spider Cakes (Quest) [item=3679 domain=www] - Blood Sausage (Quest) [b][u] These are purchasable for gold by Horde only:[/u][/b] [item=5484 domain=www] - Roasted Kodo Meat - Mulgore at 46,57 from Wunna Darkmane *There are a few recipes below obtained from Desolace, [npc=11625 domain=www] - NPC Cork Gizelton spawns in Desolace and spawns two vending machines after you follow his patrol route: one is [npc=12245 domain=www], the other is the Super-Seller 680. He can be hard to find so I recommend if you have NPCScan, clear your cache and enter ID number 11625 located in Kalimdor named Cork Gizelton. You can complete his quest while you patrol around (it takes 40 minutes for him to drop these bots!) [quest=5821 domain=www], part one of the quest gave me the following reputation (85 non-human with Mr.Popularity guild perk) (Ratchet: 275, Gadgetzan/Everlook: 138, Booty Bay: 137), part two of the quest yielded (Reputation; Ratchet: 275, Gadgetzan/Everlook: 137, Booty Bay: 13). Before starting this quest I was Honored with Ratchet and Neutral with the rest of Steamwheedle Cartel. Onwards to the recipes! [b][u]These are purchasable for gold by Horde and Alliance: [/u][/b] [item=12227 domain=www] - Lean Wolf Steak - Desolace at 40,79 from Super-Seller 680 [item=12233 domain=www] - Mystery Stew - Desolace at 40,79 from Super-Seller 680 [item=3734 domain=www] - Big Bear Steak - Desolace at 40,79 from Super-Seller 680 [item=16110 domain=www] - Monster Omelet - Winterspring at 59,51 from Himmik [item=6326 domain=www] - Slitherskin Mackerel - Durotar at 57,77 from Zansoa ([b]HORDE ONLY[/b]) [item=6326 domain=www] - Slitherskin Mackerel - Teldrassil at 54,90 from Nessa ([i]ALLIANCE ONLY[/i]) [item=6892 domain=www] - Smoked Bear Meat - Silverpine Forest at 43,40 from Andrew Hilbert ([b]HORDE ONLY[/b]) [item=6892 domain=www] - Smoked Bear Meat - Loch Modan at 35,49 from Drac Roughcut ([i]ALLIANCE ONLY[/i]) [b][u] These are obtainable by Horde and Alliance by drops or quests:[/u][/b] [item=18267 domain=www] - Runn Tunn Tuber Surprise - Dire Maul from Pusillin (73% drop) [item=2700 domain=www] - Succulent Pork Ribs - Loch Modan/Redridge Mountains drop (~1%) [i][b][u]Disclaimer: [/u][/b][/i]Some recipes may be learned from other sources than I have listed, I just found these locations to be the most convenient to access. I apologize if some of the data is incorrect or if some recipes are no longer obtainable, if this is the case please comment to let me know! Also, please feel free to add recpies that are obtainable by means other than daily commendations (reputation/vendor/trainer specific/drops). TL;DR Good Luck!"},{"id":1667985,"r":2,"n":2,"b":"I checked the Armory's \"Not Learned Yet\" feature. I have 195 recipes learned and it says I'm missing 6. 1 of those is Goldthorn Tea and I'm a mage, so that means I could possibly have exactly 200, but that includes the removed-from-game Dirge's Kickin' Chimearok Chops, so that's not happening (not available on my server anymore, and never was affordable). So the current total seems to be 199 in 4.3.3, if you are not a rogue and don't have the purple recipe. I'm not positive whether I might have other recipes that are no longer available, making the number lower for someone who started collecting after Cataclysm."},{"id":1669641,"r":2,"n":0,"b":"I just spent a few days finishing cooking dailys and farming for recipes, im currently at 199/200 and the last recipe i can get is[item=62800] My guild doesnt have many members and we are currently at 4.7k/10k for the fishing achievment, looks like i have a lot of fishing to do to get my Iron Chef, that or wait until MoP comes out."},{"id":1682413,"r":1,"n":1,"b":"I am 10 short and it would seem that searching the internet for others there are none.... Impossible to do this now?"},{"id":1691295,"r":8,"n":0,"b":"Best way to find out what your missing, check the armory.. it shows what you have and not have collected."},{"id":1692249,"r":4,"n":0,"b":"There seems to be some questions about this achieve - especially for so-called \"Cata Babies\". This [b]is[/b] still doable without the [item=21025] or even the [item=18160]; BUT, you will need to be in a Guild that has both [item=62800] and [item=62799] available from the Guild Vendor. My main is a Horde Rogue that was created (along with the account) at the start of Cataclysm. He currently has 191 recipes, and there are still 10 more available. 2 of those remaining recipes are purchasable only by Alliance, and the remaining 8 are from the Day of the Dead, Pilgrim's Bounty and Winter Veil world events."},{"id":1724144,"r":1,"n":1,"b":"Does anyone know if this is account wide ? i.e if i have several toons with cooking awards and spend them on diffrent recepies or do i have to grind it all on one toon ?"},{"id":1737654,"r":-5,"n":0,"b":"All of us spent all that time to get a total of 200 recipes, which was virtually impossible, and then with mists we had them pretty much right away (along with the achievement). But we no longer get the title of \"Iron Chef\" which would have been a pretty rare on server. Bummer!"},{"id":1882680,"r":8,"n":0,"b":"there's a bit of confusion about these achievements, if you have not learned 200 pre-MoP recipes yet, the MoP recipes that you learn at halfhill will not make your counter go up on your tracker but they still count towards the cooking recipes achievements, once you have learned 200 pre-MoP recipes you will get ([achievement=5471]) and your counter will jump to the actual total amount or recipes you have including MoP recipes"},{"id":1930150,"r":2,"n":0,"b":"This guy [npc=340 domain=www] has some of the recipes you get from quests."},{"id":2032957,"r":4,"n":0,"b":"All of these count for your 200 recipes for [url=http://www.wowhead.com/achievement=5471/iron-chef]Iron Chef[/url] if you never finished it: [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111356/fishing-guide-to-draenor]Fishing Guide to Draenor[/url] [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111364]First Aid in Draenor[/url] [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111387]The Joy of Draenor Cooking[/url] [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111350]A Compendium of the Herbs of Draenor[/url] [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111349]A Treatise on Mining in Draenor[/url] [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=111351]A Guide to Skinning in Draenor[/url] I was tracking the achievement and was shocked that I got it when I went over 200 recipes with these non-cooking recipes.
